messages:
jamal: noticed a surge of 403s on /v1/embeddings starting ~04:02 UTC, looks tied to the scheduled rewrap for kms-key-7
priya: yep, customers reported failures and spikes in retries/latency, currently sending an INCIDENT banner
cheng: authz logs show scope check failures — tokens coming back with 'models:chat' tag only when calling embeddings route. sample: 
```
[04:03:11] authz ERROR tok=tok_9f3 check=scope_mismatch route=/v1/embeddings token_tags=["models:chat"]
```
opsbot: nightly-rewrap-0 completed for kms-key-7 at 04:00:58 UTC (stepdown sequence)
maria: digging into KMS + identity-service traces: the tag-write step hit a 504 at 04:01:59 while persisting per-token scope metadata
jamal: reproduction: curl using rotated token -> 403 for /v1/embeddings, but same token succeeds on /v1/chat
priya: mitigation brainstorm: short-term allowlist to accept chat-scoped tokens on embeddings endpoints until we reconcile? I know it's not ideal for least-privilege
cheng: strong -1 on that. We should avoid broadening permissions. Prefer rollback of the rewrap or a targeted reconciliation of token tags
maria: agree with Cheng. Likely root: rewrap marked success but per-token tag writes partially failed due to identity-service timeout, leaving tokens with stale/partial metadata
jamal: quick fix options: 1) pause further rewrap jobs 2) rollback rewrap for kms-key-7 if we can 3) route embeddings traffic to older cluster without rewrap applied while we fix
priya: ops is already spinning up traffic redirect to the legacy scope-checker cluster as hot-path mitigation
opsbot: emergency routing change applied to cluster-2 at 04:20 UTC
cheng: code snippet from authz hot-path that made this visible:
```
def is_allowed(token, route):
  scopes = token.metadata.get('scopes', [])
  if not scopes:
    scopes = fetch_legacy_tag_sync(token.id)
  return route.required_scope in scopes
```
cheng: the sync fetch against legacy index during rotation is brittle; it amplified the outage when identity-service was slow
maria: KMS audit shows rewrap job's final status succeeded, but the per-token tag write log entries are incomplete around 04:01-04:02 UTC
priya: customer impact estimate: roughly a dozen customers experienced repeated 403s for ~10-15 minutes; billing unaffected but app UX degraded
jamal: proposed immediate checklist:
- pause all scheduled rewraps globally
- run targeted reconcile to reapply missing token tags for key-7
- add a post-success verification that reads back tag writes per-token before marking rewrap success
- change authz to fail-closed and emit a distinct audit event when scopes are missing
- avoid synchronous legacy-tag fetch on hot path (switch to async/queued enrich or cached fallback)
maria: I'll own the KMS tag reconciliation script and a verification runbook
cheng: I'll prepare a small authz patch to fail-closed and add clearer audit fields (token_id, key_id, rewrap_tx_id) — aiming for staging deploy in ~40m
priya: I'll draft the customer-facing message. Suggested line: "We observed an identity-service timeout during scheduled KMS metadata rewrap which caused scope tags to be missing on some API tokens, leading to rejected embeddings requests. No key material or plaintext was exposed."
deploy-bot: authz/patch-rewrap-audit deployed to staging at 05:02 UTC
jamal: once patch validated in staging, we can rollback the routing detour and restore normal traffic
cheng: longer-term follow-ups: add per-token tag-write metrics (count failures per rewrap), gating canary for rewrap that validates a subset of tokens end-to-end, and an alert if embeddings 403 rate > 0.5% after any rewrap
maria: also recommend updating the runbook: if embeddings 403 spike after key rotation -> check identity-service write latency, compare KMS rewrap success vs per-token tag confirmations, consider immediate rollback and reconcile
priya: filed INC-2026-48 and assigning postmortem owner; will update customers and internal runbook notes after the hotfix
jamal: thanks all — big props for moving quickly :thumbsup: 
priya: will circulate the postmortem draft later today and tag eng-sre, platform, and infra for the follow-ups
